ShortDescription.Value: Build one city together over a dedicated server. Roads, zoning, terrain, policies, progression and mod settings sync live; a small server program holds the shared city on your PC or on a Linux box.

Publish.LongDescription:
Build one city with friends. A small server program holds the shared city and passes round what everyone does; the game talks to it through this mod. Run the server from your own PC with one click, or put it on a Linux or Windows box and leave it running for your group.
**What syncs live** - Roads, buildings, zoning, bulldozing, terrain, districts and transit lines appear on everyone's screen as they are placed. You also see the other players' tool ghosts: the road they are dragging out, the building under their cursor, the area they are drawing. - Taxes, budgets, service fees, city policies and building options. - Progression: a development node one player buys is bought for everyone, and the host's XP and development points are shared, so milestones arrive together. - One treasury. The host's balance is the city's balance. - Where everyone is: a ring where each player is looking, a dot under their mouse, their name over it. - Other mods' settings: Traffic Tool Essentials junction settings, the Traffic mod's lane connections and priority signs, and Road Builder's custom roads.
Farms, forestry, mines and oil fields are the one thing not sent live yet; they arrive with the next save.
**How a session works** Main menu > **Multiplayer**. **Host game** starts the server window next to your game and joins it; friends join your address and port (27015 unless you change it, forwarded on your router). **Join game** connects to a friend or to a dedicated server. Joining from the menu downloads the shared city and loads it.
In a city, the round button at the top of the right-hand stack opens the panel: save to the server, fetch the newer city, see who is on. Anyone can save. The host also saves on its own every few minutes, and whoever joins later gets the latest save.
When the host connects and the server already holds a city, the game asks: load last save, or new world. New world opens the map list, mod maps included, and the city you start replaces the one on the server.
The simulation itself still runs on each PC, so citizens and traffic are not identical everywhere. Everything you build is.
**Dedicated server** This is a dedicated-server mod. The server is a separate program, not the game, so it runs on a box without Cities: Skylines II installed. The same program that Host game opens is on GitHub as a download for Linux and Windows, with an install script that sets it up as a service. All settings sit in one server.json file (name, password, owner key, mod check, welcome message) and the server picks up edits on its own. It can follow a public Paradox playset and tell anyone it turns away exactly which mods they are missing, and it checks GitHub for newer releases.
Server downloads, source code and issues: github.com/DillanStephenson/Cities-Skylines-2---multiplayer-DEDICATED-SERVER
**Mods** Any mod is fine as long as everyone runs the same playset. The server compares mod lists, ignoring version numbers, and tells a rejected player which playset to activate.
**Credits** Made by Dillan Stephenson. Testing: Mayor William. Thanks to the makers of Traffic Tool Essentials, Traffic and Road Builder, whose mods this one learned to carry along.
Early access: play with people you know, keep your own saves, and report problems on GitHub.
Publish.ChangeLog: 0.3.7: Closes a hole opened by the retries in 0.3.6. When another player's build was put back to be tried again, the pieces the game had already made from it were left lying in your city with nothing owning them, and your game could then send them out again as though you had built them. That is the old "it is placing things for my friend" fault, and it is now impossible: every path that abandons a build clears up after itself. 0.3.6: Your game no longer builds half of what someone else placed. When part of another player's build is not valid here, the whole thing is held and tried again for a few seconds, and only if it still will not go does it give up and say so. Before, the valid parts were built anyway, which left half a road or a building with no approach, and everything placed near it afterwards then collided with the mess. The panel and the log also now show a full tally of every build that has arrived: replayed, batched, part-built, retried, given up, waiting. The numbers add up, so a problem cannot hide. 0.3.5: More desync repairs, all found by auditing the mod against a real two-player session. Junction lane connections are checked before anything is touched: a change that could not be applied used to delete the junction's settings first and then give up, and the wreckage was then sent to everyone else. An empty set of lane connections no longer reads as "clear this junction", which could wipe the other player's work the moment the Traffic mod created a junction. Taxes, budgets, fees and policies set by anyone other than the host are no longer swallowed: the host's money update every five seconds was quietly cancelling them. A custom road that has been edited is sent again, so both PCs stop building with different shapes under the same name. Farm, forestry, mine and oil areas: edits to them are now held back like their creation, instead of being sent to a PC that never received the area. And the drift check now counts the one thing that really proves two cities have gone out of step, a build the game here refuses part of, which it used to ignore completely. 0.3.4: The big one for desync. Three faults were switching whole features off silently. Saving to the server on a timer and "Sync everyone every N minutes" never ran once: they compared two different clocks, so the timer never came due. Builds that arrived while your game was loading the shared city were replayed into it afterwards, building everything a second time on top of itself, which is where the overlap errors came from. And a game waiting for a fresh save that never came would throw away every build for the rest of the session; it now gives up after two minutes and carries on. Also: a build that cannot find what it attaches to is retried for ten seconds instead of dropped, so one missing road no longer takes everything built on it with it; matching a building can no longer pick a passing car or a pedestrian; and something sixty metres below is no longer a valid match for something above it. Fixes a fault in 0.3.3 where your own builds were not sent if you picked a tool while another player's build was landing. 0.3.3: Joining a city others are already playing asks them for a fresh save first and fetches that (it waits up to a minute), instead of the last upload, so nothing built since is missing on your side. "Reload when someone else saves" is gone: a plain save no longer makes the others reload, which threw away everything built after that save started; only the group sync and a drift resync reload a running game. Another player's build never takes your tool while you hold the mouse button (a road being dragged, zones being painted), and a click during the brief moment the selection tool stands in does nothing instead of selecting something; nothing another player built can go back out as yours. 0.3.2: Fixes the "+25 XP Electricity network online" (and population bonus) popping up every few seconds on everyone but the host: sharing the host's XP wiped the game's record of bonuses already paid, so it paid them again. Other players' builds no longer make your toolbar and tool options flash: the short switch to the selection tool while their build lands is now invisible to the UI. Saves to the server go through the game's own save queue; saving outside it could collide with the game's autosave and throw a null reference in the serializer, which is what one player hit. 0.2.3 to 0.2.9: first published build and the run-up to 0.3.0 — server window and shared city, live build sync, city settings and shared treasury, player markers, playset-aware mod check, Traffic Tool Essentials and Traffic and Road Builder settings syncing, tool ghosts, progression sync, and the New city / load-or-new-world flow.
